claim: Learned-vs-quantum MAE diverges with parent-molecule size in C-H bonds: at HAC>=10 learned MAE 3.2458 vs quantum 2.2016 (n=146), while at HAC<=5 learned 1.7304 vs quantum 1.7571 (n=52), and this cross-over makes the overall learned-minus-quantum edge of 0.31 kcal/mol fragile.
value_found: C-H HAC>=10: learned 3.2458219178, quantum 2.2016438356, n=146 (claimed 3.2458/2.2016/n=146 - exact match). C-H HAC<=5: learned 1.7303846154, quantum 1.7571153846, n=52 (claimed 1.7304/1.7571/n=52 - exact match). Overall learned-minus-quantum MAE edge 0.3128913444 (claimed 0.31). Slice edges: HAC>=10 +1.0442 (paired t=4.365, p=2.40e-05; bootstrap 95% CI [0.5905,1.5294]); HAC<=5 -0.0267 (paired t=-0.580, p=0.564; bootstrap CI [-0.1194,0.0583], includes 0). Interaction difference-of-differences = 1.0709 (Welch t=4.396, p=2.04e-05; 20000-draw permutation p=0.0074). Overall edge excluding HAC>=10 = -0.0181 (CI [-0.0999,0.0653]). UNIT SENSITIVITY: unique C-H molecules, HAC>=10 n=144 learned 3.2851 vs quantum 2.2249; HAC<=5 n=42 learned 1.7150 vs quantum 1.7252. Molecule-mean aggregation: 3.2628 vs 2.2035 (n=144) and 1.8166 vs 1.8262 (n=42). C-C replicates the same sign pattern: HAC>=10 learned 4.2750 vs quantum 3.8235 (n=46), HAC<=5 learned 1.4480 vs quantum 1.6074 (n=61). BOILERPLATE claim 5 (both methods, independent): method A near-duplicate pairs |dQ|<=0.1, n_pairs=1002, sigma=2.843664 (ddof=0 gives 2.853856); method B moment decomposition [V(E-Q)+V(E-L)-V(Q-L)]/2 = 8.026105 sqrt=2.833038; methods agree to 0.021 kcal/mol (0.7%). Oracle MAE sqrt(2/pi)*sigma = 2.2604. BOILERPLATE claim 11: correct pooled within-molecule SD = sqrt(sum (n_g-1)s_g^2 / sum(n_g-1)) = 9.965372 (9.97), 419 molecules, 86 multi-row, spreads mean 13.4186 / median 11.90 / max 47.90 - all exact. The ~165 figure is NOT produced by any ordinary naive pooling: ddof-0 n-weighted = 10.110236, unweighted mean-of-variances = 10.315528, sqrt(sum of variances) = 95.662271; it is reproduced only by squaring the per-group variances inside the weighted average, sqrt(avg((s_g^2)^2, weights=n_g-1)) = 165.2622713. That is a variance-squared slip, not a ddof/weighting artifact.
unit: Bond observation (raw benchmark row, 543 total), parent-molecule heavy-atom count (HAC) computed from parent_structure_smiles; C-H class assigned from fragment radical centres. For C-H bonds the fragment heavy-atom sum is numerically identical to parent HAC (H contributes 0 heavy atoms; 0/302 rows differ), so the two size definitions coincide here. Slice n=146 and n=52 are bond observations, correctly labelled; the unique-molecule equivalents are n=144 and n=42.
method: Own scripts, no import of common.py or any workstream script: (1) python /data/user/conversations/conv-75e3fc1d-c4c9-41b5-800b-05f4632eec99/project/output/results/_verify9_indep.py - reads experimental_benchmark.tsv directly, computes HAC with RDKit, labels bond class from radical centres, forms |learned-exp| and |quantum-exp|, slices by HAC; (2) _verify9_probe.py - unit sensitivity, bootstrap CIs, paired t, difference-of-differences interaction test with Welch t and 20000-draw permutation, leave-out decomposition of the overall 0.31 edge; (3) _verify9_sens.py - cut-point sensitivity (HAC>=8..12 and <=3..7), per-HAC-value edges, Spearman/Pearson of HAC vs per-observation error difference, DB domain membership by HAC stratum; (4) _verify9_robust.py - median/trimmed/p90 errors, leave-one-molecule-out influence, out-of-DB vs in-DB size gradients; (5) _verify9_boiler.py - methods A and B for the reference sigma and pooled within-molecule SD with naive-formula variants. Raw outputs: output/results/_verify9_raw.json, _verify9_probe.json, _verify9_sens.json, _verify9_robust.json, _verify9_boiler.json.
notes: All four reported numbers and both n's reproduce to the last printed digit, and the cross-over direction is robust across analysis units (bond observation, unique molecule, molecule-mean) and across the C-H and C-C bond classes. MEDIAN AND TRIMMED ERRORS PRESERVE THE GAP, so it is not an outlier artifact: HAC>=10 C-H median AE learned 2.445 vs quantum 1.840, 10%-trimmed 2.842 vs 1.930; leave-one-molecule-out learned MAE stays in [3.168, 3.279] and dropping the 5 worst observations still leaves 2.936 vs 2.251. KEY CONFOUND (does not refute the numbers but qualifies the 'molecule size' reading): the database's own HAC maximum is exactly 10, so HAC>10 is perfectly collinear with extrapolation beyond the database domain - all 150 benchmark observations with parent HAC>10 are outside the database, and within the C-H HAC>=10 slice 124/146 rows are HAC>10 while only 22 are HAC==10. The HAC==10 C-H cell alone (n=22) shows learned 2.495 vs quantum 2.439, an edge of only +0.056, so the +1.044 slice edge is carried by the out-of-domain HAC>10 rows. The divergence is therefore equally well described as database-domain extrapolation as by molecular size; the two factors cannot be separated with these data. Within the out-of-database C-H stratum the edge nevertheless still rises with HAC (6-9: +0.406, 10-13: +0.364, 14+: +1.687), so it is not purely a membership flag effect. The claim's characterisation of the HAC<=5 side as 'slightly BETTER' is numerically correct but statistically a null (-0.027, p=0.56, CI includes 0), and it is cut-point sensitive: the edge flips sign at HAC<=6 (+0.083) and HAC<=7 (+0.113), so only the <=5 (and <=3/<=4) cut gives the 'learned better' side. The 'fragile overall edge' interpretation is supported by leave-out: the HAC>=10 stratum has 35.5% of rows and contributes +0.3246 of the +0.3129 overall edge; excluding it the overall edge becomes -0.0181 (CI [-0.0999, 0.0653]). Row counts: the benchmark is 543 unique (molecule, fragment_a, fragment_b) observations over 419 unique parents; the claim's n=146/n=52 are correct bond-observation counts. Boilerplate claim-5 methods A and B agree within 0.021 kcal/mol (2.8437 vs 2.8330), both matching their reported values; claim-11's correct pooled within-molecule SD is 9.9654 (reported 9.97) and the ~165 figure is reproducible only as a squared-variance artifact (165.2623), confirming it is a coding slip rather than a legitimate alternative pooling.
